redlining.def: Refusing loans, insurance or other services, or offering worse terms, based on a property's location; in US history it was aimed mostly at Black and immigrant neighborhoods.

blockbusting.def: A practice in which real estate agents scared white owners into selling cheaply by claiming Black families were moving in, then resold the homes at higher prices; outlawed in the United States in 1968.

gentrification.def: The movement of higher-income residents and investment into a lower-income neighborhood, raising property values and often displacing long-time renters.

urban-renewal.def: A government program that buys, clears and rebuilds areas judged to be run-down, often displacing the people who lived there.

disamenity-zone.def: One of the poorest, least-served parts of a city, such as an area of abandoned buildings or of unsafe land where the newest arrivals settle.

inclusionary-zoning.def: A zoning policy that requires or rewards developers for including homes priced for lower- and middle-income households in new buildings.

environmental-injustice.def: The unequal burden of pollution and environmental harm on poor and minority communities.
